results.evidence: The published route description for this Washington peak is a cross-country hike from Lyman Lake across meadow then Class 2 talus/scree on the south side, a little over 4 mi round trip and ~2,600 ft from the lake. The 'East Ridge ... Magnolia Mine' text matches the standard East Ridge route of the unrelated 13,614 ft North Star Mountain in Colorado, where the Magnolia Mine claims sit on the ridge approach - copied from the wrong peak. WTA confirms the Washington peak is reached by off-trail scrambling from the Lyman Lakes/Cloudy Pass trail area with no summit trail.

results.fact: Crevasse/glacier-travel hazard on the Spider Gap approach
results.correct_value: No glacier travel on the climb itself, but the current Spider Gap approach climbs a permanent snowfield/small glacier to the gap and descends a steep, often snowy path toward Upper Lyman Lake; an ice axe is recommended.
results.evidence: WTA's Spider Gap description says an ice axe or poles are highly recommended for climbing up the Spider Glacier to the ~7,100 ft gap, and that the boot path down toward Upper Lyman Lakes can be treacherous when snow- or ice-covered. A 2019 trip report describes the permanent snowfield on the gap's south side and a large melt hole on the descent. So 'N/A - no glacier travel' is wrong for the route as it is reached now, but the summit climb itself has no glacier.

results.fact: trailhead and pass used by the standard route
results.correct_value: There are two genuine approaches. (1) North Fork Entiat Trailhead (end of FR 5606) up Trail #1437 to the Pyramid junction/Fox Camp, over Saska Pass, down into the Snow Brushy burn and up to the crest saddle just south of the peak - this is the line the route's waypoints, map and approach variant follow, so it goes on the trailhead card. (2) Entiat River Trailhead near Cottonwood, 7 mi up the Entiat River Trail to the 45-Mile Sheep Driveway, then off-trail via Aurora Creek into the Pinnacle Creek drainage below Borealis Ridge to the same saddle. There is no 'Emerald Park' on either line, and neither ascends 'via Borealis Pass'.
results.evidence: One published guide describes the Entiat River Trail route: 7 mi to the 45-Mile Sheep Driveway, off-trail via Aurora Creek into Pinnacle Creek, camps at 6,500/7,200/7,600 ft on Borealis Ridge, then easy south slopes from the saddle south of Pinnacle on the Chelan Mountains crest. Borealis Pass appears only on its day-2 exit toward Choral Mountain. Two independent 'Chelan Slam' trip reports start from the North Fork Entiat Trailhead, pass the Pyramid Mountain trail junction, and camp at the head of the North Fork. One crosses the Saska saddle, drops over 1,000 ft through the burn and climbs a gully to Pinnacle. So both approaches are real. The itinerary's 'Emerald Park' is wrong for both, and the row's 'Borealis Pass' ascent references are wrong. The fix sets the trailhead card to match the waypoints and labels the itinerary as the Entiat River Trail option.
